items.prompt: A caller removes the cent-grid and magnitude guarantees but keeps arbitrary float inputs. May the recovery claim still be used?

options.text: No, the original integer cents may no longer be uniquely recoverable.
options.why: The guarantee depends on both the grid and the bounded float error.

options.text: Yes, float retains every decimal digit at every magnitude.
options.why: Finite binary precision does not retain arbitrary decimal information.

options.text: Yes, multiplying by 100 reconstructs digits that were already lost.
options.why: Scaling cannot restore information discarded by the original float conversion.

options.text: No, because the valid bounded task never accepts any floats.
options.why: It does accept starter-produced floats under the explicit bounded recovery argument.

items.explanation: The guarantee depends on both the grid and the bounded float error.
